description: Lists what a custom automation on one WhatsApp number can be built from: each thing it can start on, with the settings it takes and the conditions it can start on; each step it can take, with the inputs it takes and what it returns; each integration working for that number, with its actions and their inputs; and the JSON Schema of the automation document, with the operators and functions a condition is written in. Only what the workspace’s plan includes and the number’s working integrations allow is listed. Read-only: it runs nothing and changes nothing.

connection_id.description: The WhatsApp number (connection id) the automation is for: only what can be built and run on it is listed.

name: list_automation_building_blocks

input_schema.description: The JSON Schema of what the step takes, with the recipe forms’ `picker` where an input is one (`tag`, `template`, `language`, `sheet`, `account`). A send’s `to` is `picker: "recipient"`, with two `choices`: `customer`, “The customer who wrote”, which binds `binds` (`{ "kind": "ref", "path": "contact.id" }`) and is offered, and chosen first, on the starts its `starts` lists; and `number`, “A fixed number”, typed with its country code as its `description` says. Validate refuses a send with neither (`missing_recipient`) and a number the phone rule refuses (`unusable_recipient`), in plain words naming the step, at `<step>/inputs/to`. Every other input naming one contact is `picker: "contact"`, with the same two `choices`, refused as `missing_contact` and `unusable_contact`; every input naming a chat is `picker: "conversation"`, with one `choice`, `chat`, “This chat”, which binds `{ "kind": "ref", "path": "conversation.id" }` and is offered, and chosen first, on the starts its `starts` lists, refused left empty as `missing_conversation`. Each refusal is at `<step>/inputs/<input>`.

outcomes.description: The named outcomes this block may end with besides working or failing, each with the causes it gives. A split block maps one to a branch (`{ "type": "outcome", "step", "is", "cause" }`). Empty for a block that only works or fails.

test_reads_for_real.description: The integration actions a Test runs for real through this block: reads, each marked so one by one. Every other integration action is held back in a Test, whatever it does. Empty for every block but “Call an integration”; any other block runs in a Test only when its `side_effect` is `none`.

unavailable_reason.description: Why the block cannot be used, in one plain sentence an owner reads: the sentence validate refuses it with at save. `null` when `available` is true.

document_schema.description: The JSON Schema of an automation document (`ir_version` 1.0): what it starts on, its steps (actions, conditions, branches, loops, waits) and the expressions a condition is written in, each operator and function by name. Present when `connection_id` names a number.

integrations.description: Every integration that has actions, with them: what a “Call an integration” step can name as its `integration` and `action`, and what each takes and answers.

action.description: The action’s key: what the step names as `action`.

description.description: What the action does, in plain words. `null` when it declares none.

destructive.description: Whether it deletes or cancels something that cannot be got back. A step that calls it is confirmed by the name `integration.call:<integration>.<action>` before the automation is switched on, and data a stranger controls may not decide whether it runs.

input_schema.description: The JSON Schema of the step’s `input`: a field with a default may be left out.

output_schema.description: The JSON Schema of what the action answers, which the step returns as `result`. `null` when the action does not declare it.

test_reads_for_real.description: Whether a Test runs it for real: a read, marked so. Every other action is held back in a Test.

integration.description: The integration’s key: what a “Call an integration” step names as `integration`.

answers.description: Whether the trigger can carry `answers` (what of a customer’s message the automation claims). Only `whatsapp.message_received` can.

filters.description: The checks on the event a builder offers on this start, each optional (“From contains”). Each is one clause of the trigger’s `filters.only_when`: `clause`, with the owner’s value as a `lit` where the `param` named `name` stands. Several are one `{ "kind": "op", "op": "and", "args": [...] }`. They are decided before a run exists: an event they keep out is not run and counts nothing (its run is `skipped`, `filtered`). Only `email.received` has any: `from_contains` and `subject_contains`, matched in any case, and `label`, a Gmail label matched exactly (the owner’s by name, Gmail’s own by id, such as `STARRED`). Empty on every other trigger.

about.description: What a field means, in one line, by its path below the subtree (`reply_to.params`).

nested.description: A field a step may read into, by name: its own fields, and those of them (`open`) whose values are by any name, read one level further (`message.reply_to.params.<variable>`).

params_schema.description: The JSON Schema of the trigger’s `params`: exactly the ones it accepts, each with a plain `description`, `required` naming the ones it needs, and the recipe forms’ `picker` where a param is one (`tag`, `account`, `form`, `sheet`, `tab`). On a start an integration delivers, `account` also has `connectors`: the keys of the integrations whose accounts it starts on, the ones switching on binds, listing the integrations this workspace can connect; so do `form_id`, `spreadsheet_id` and `sheet`, with the integrations whose trigger takes that setting. An empty object schema when it takes none. Validate refuses any other param, and a needed one left out, at `/trigger/params/<name>`.

start_if.description: The start conditions the trigger takes in `filters.start_if`: a list of `{ "type": … }`, and it starts if ANY is met. An event that meets none is not run and counts nothing (its run is `skipped`, `filtered`). On `whatsapp.message_received` (four that read the message) and `contact.tagged` (`not_asked_for_review`); absent on every other trigger.

title: List automation building blocks
